finding.claim: The admin listener exposes unauthenticated KV write/delete endpoints (PUT/DELETE /api/kv/{store}/{key}); any client that can reach admin_addr can mutate KV stores that the filter pipeline may read.
finding.source: Any network client that can reach the admin_addr TCP listener (no credentials required). Request method PUT or DELETE with path /api/kv/{store}/{key}.

trace.note: add_admin_endpoints_to_pingora_server binds admin_addr with service.add_tcp (plain TCP, no TLS, no auth layer).
PingoraAdminService::response reads the path and performs no authentication or authorization check.
Paths starting with /api/kv/ are dispatched directly to dispatch_kv_request when kv_registry is Some.
dispatch_kv_request resolves the route from method and path, with no identity check.
KvRoute::Set reads the request body via read_body.
handle_set calls backend.set(key, value) and returns 200 on success.
KvRoute::Delete calls handle_delete, which calls backend.delete(key).

finding.guards_checked: Body cap of 1 MiB (kv/mod.rs:25, 129-131); UTF-8 validation (kv/mod.rs:142-145); 404 for unknown store (kv/mod.rs:154-156, 170-171); route validation of exactly two segments (kv/mod.rs:92-107); JSON escaping on read paths (service.rs:36-54; kv/mod.rs:159-161, 202-208). NOT present in this code: authentication, authorization, TLS, or any restriction of admin_addr to loopback. The default and configured bind address are in config code that is not in this directory, so exploitability depends on that config.

finding.claim: After a WebSocket upgrade, request and response body filters are skipped entirely, including the SizeLimit enforcement. Frames sent over the tunnel are not inspected by body-level filters.
finding.source: Client request with Upgrade: websocket and Connection: Upgrade. The upstream answers 101 Switching Protocols with Upgrade: websocket, which sets ctx.connection_upgraded.
finding.sink: Body filter pipeline (execute_http_request_body) and SizeLimit check (check_body_size_limit) are bypassed for the rest of the connection (request_body_filter.rs:41-43, 63-73; response_body_filter.rs:38).

trace.note: A 101 from upstream is rejected unless the request carried an Upgrade header (request_has_upgrade).
is_upgrade_response is true only if the 101 has an Upgrade value that is exactly websocket (hop_by_hop.rs:73-75).
ctx.connection_upgraded is set from is_upgrade_response.
execute() returns Ok immediately when connection_upgraded is set, before pre-read, SizeLimit, and pipeline execution.
Same early return for response body filters.

finding.guards_checked: 101 must follow a client upgrade request and must be websocket-only (response_filter.rs:40-47). h2c and mixed Upgrade values are stripped (upstream_request.rs:33-43, hop_by_hop.rs:61-75). Upgraded connections still get header-phase filters. Nothing in this code gates whether body filters should run on WebSocket frames. Whether the bypass matters depends on which body-inspection filters are configured, and those are not in this directory. Confidence medium: the behavior is clear from the code, the intent is not documented here.

finding.claim: Client-controlled Connection tokens remove any upstream-bound header by name, including headers the filter pipeline set in request_filter. A client can make a trusted pipeline-injected header disappear before it reaches the backend.
finding.source: Request header Connection: <name> where <name> matches a header the pipeline set (for example an identity or auth-result header inserted by a filter).
finding.sink: Upstream request header set (strip_connection_tokens calls remove_header_by_name; upstream_request.rs:41-43, hop_by_hop.rs:91-105).

trace.note: Pipeline headers_to_set and extra_headers are inserted into session.req_header_mut() during request_filter.
upstream_request_filter runs after request_filter and calls strip_hop_by_hop(upstream_request, is_upgrade) (line 183). with_body.rs:218-219 does the same.
strip_hop_by_hop snapshots every Connection value (hop_by_hop.rs:83-85) without distinguishing client-supplied headers from pipeline-set ones.
strip_connection_tokens removes each token that is not in the static hop-by-hop list (lines 98-103).

finding.guards_checked: Static hop-by-hop list (hop_by_hop.rs:24-33). Reserved-name rejection covers only x-praxis-* and x-ext-protocol-*/x-ext-agent-* prefixes (request_filter/mod.rs:75-78; reserved_headers.rs:20-22). It does not cover arbitrary names a filter may set. Impact depends on backend behavior when the header is missing (for example fail-open to anonymous) and on the filters, which are not in this directory. Confidence medium.

finding.claim: obs-fold unfolding replaces every value of a repeated header with one unfolded value, silently dropping the other values of that header.
finding.source: Request with a repeated header (for example two Cookie or X-Forwarded-For lines) where at least one value contains CRLF followed by SP or HTAB.
finding.sink: Forwarded request header map integrity: sibling values are lost (normalize.rs:163 insert_header).

trace.note: handle_obs_fold runs from normalize_request_headers (line 63).
headers_snapshot collects each (name, value) pair whose value contains obs-fold and whose name is not in OBS_FOLD_REJECT_HEADERS.
insert_header(name, new_value) overwrites all existing values for that name (http::HeaderMap::insert semantics). Sibling values that do not contain obs-fold are lost.

finding.guards_checked: Host and Content-Length with obs-fold are rejected (normalize.rs:142-149). Conflicting duplicate Content-Length and Content-Type are rejected (normalize.rs:75-99). The loss of sibling values is not guarded. Impact is integrity only (silent value loss). Confidence medium-high; assumes Pingora's insert_header behaves like HeaderMap::insert, which is not in this directory.

finding.claim: Transfer-Encoding is not in the obs-fold rejection list, and normalization does not check Transfer-Encoding together with Content-Length. Header framing is normalized after Pingora has parsed the request, so the proxy's view of framing and the normalized header view can differ.
finding.source: Request with obs-fold inside Transfer-Encoding, or with both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length present.
finding.sink: Request framing and body-length decisions (Pingora parser and body reader, not in this directory). The proxy-side effect is limited because Transfer-Encoding is stripped before the upstream request (hop_by_hop.rs:24-33).

trace.note: OBS_FOLD_REJECT_HEADERS lists only Host and Content-Length.
normalize_request_headers checks only duplicate CL/CT and obs-fold. It has no TE/CL conflict check.
Obs-fold in Transfer-Encoding is unfolded (not rejected) into a single-line value.
normalize runs in request_filter, after Pingora has already parsed the request and decided body framing.

finding.guards_checked: Pingora's own HTTP/1 parser (not in this directory) may already reject TE+CL and obs-fold. Whether it does is not verifiable here. Upstream TE stripping (hop_by_hop.rs:24-33) limits proxy-to-backend desync. Confidence low; this is a candidate for manual review of the Pingora parser configuration, not a confirmed smuggling issue.
